text:
alex: Heads up — noticed a suspicious child process named 'runc-helper' spawning inside a runtime container on prod-ml-01 around 08:12 UTC. Container hasn't been restarted. Can someone take point on evidence collection + KMS/audit correlation? tagging @nisha @leo :eyes:
sara: Don’t touch the container or restart the pod. Quick evidence steps I’d run now (I can do them if someone hands node access):
```
# on node (kubectl exec if needed)
kubectl -n prod exec -it pod/prod-ml-01 -- ps aux --forest | grep runc-helper
kubectl -n prod cp pod/prod-ml-01:/proc/$(pgrep -f runc-helper)/cmdline ./cmdline.dump
kubectl -n prod exec pod/prod-ml-01 -- cat /proc/$(pgrep -f runc-helper)/environ > environ.dump
kubectl -n prod exec pod/prod-ml-01 -- ls -la /proc/$(pgrep -f runc-helper)/cwd
# capture container FS overlay metadata
docker inspect --format '{{.GraphDriver}}' <container-id> || ctr containers info <cid>
```
jamie: +1 to leaving it running. Also snapshot the node and take a disk image if possible (don't delete overlay files). If we suspect image tampering, verify image digest and cosign attestation before any restart: we should not redeploy until registry check is done.
michael: For registry/attestations, run: `crane manifest ${REG}/repo@sha256:...` and `cosign verify --keyless ${REG}/repo@sha256:...` — we need to know if the image was swapped after pull. Also pull logs from our image signer (KMS envelope logs) for any sign events around yesterday 22:00-23:30 UTC.
eng-sre-bot: Incident created: SEC-2026-1072 — auto-captured node metrics + pod logs archived to s3://redwood-incidents/SEC-2026-1072/ (files: metrics.tar.gz, pod-prod-ml-01-logs.gz).
nisha: Oncall here. I’ll start audit correlation: registry access logs, artifact signing events, and KMS envelope logs. Questions: who pulled the image and with what SA? @leo can you give a fast wildcard of pulls for that digest? Also, if the container holds any mounted secrets (project-keystore), treat them as potentially exfiltrated and rotate ASAP.
leo: Registry side — I can see pulls for digest sha256:4fae... by service-account ml-inferencer@prod between 07:58-08:05 UTC from 3 different nodes. Also a pull from flow-checker@ci at 03:02 UTC. No pushes recorded in that window. I'll dump the auth token audit (who minted tokens) in 10m.
claire: Infra note: if we decide to rebuild and re-sign, we should follow the minimal rebuild flow: base-image rebuild -> run integration smoke on staging -> cosign resign with KMS signing key -> canary rollout with traffic ramp. Recommend holding full production redeploy to the evening window (22:00 UTC) unless we find active exploitation.
alex: Action items — (1) sara to capture the proc dumps and filesystem metadata (2) leo to provide token audit and pull list (3) nisha to correlate KMS/signing logs and open any key-rotation if needed (4) jamie/claire to plan fast rebuild/resign path and hold canary. I’ll be onlead for the postmortem and will coordinate customer-impact comms if any.
sara: Started capture, pushing artifacts to incident bucket now: s3://redwood-incidents/SEC-2026-1072/evidence/. Uploaded files: cmdline.dump, environ.dump, container-metadata.json, proc-tree.txt.
michael: I found that cosign verify fails for that digest with keyless verification — `verification failed: no matching signatures found`. Could be missing attestation or the image was pulled from a mirror that strips signatures. Adding that to the triage list.
nisha: If cosign fails, treat as tamper suspicion. Temporarily revoke the registry read token used by ml-inferencer@prod and switch pods to a static signed image (if you can) or put an admission policy to block that digest. I'll create a RBAC change PR to tighten who can request short-lived tokens for registry pulls.
leo: Revoked token for ml-inferencer@prod and created a scoped token for canary host only. Also flagged the CI token for review.
jamie: Forensics note — check kernel audit (auditd) for execve of that binary, and container runtime logs for `runc` invocation. Also snapshot `/var/lib/docker/overlay2` for the container layer.
claire: Scheduling: I’ll block the 22:00 UTC deploy window and prep a rebuild playbook. If we need emergency rebuild earlier, we’ll follow the fast path but require nisha + leo signoff.
alex: Good. Please put short updates here so I can track. I’ll file the incident ticket and draft an initial incident timeline. Thanks all :thumbsup:
